correctness.rationale: Every hypothesis is explicit: a>=3,b>=2, single edge within the a-shore, simple undirected adjacency and synchronous self-exclusive F_2 neighbor XOR. Four independent input functionals prove rank(F)=4, and the invariant 4-dimensional image is represented by M_{alpha,beta} in RESULT.md. Its four rank sequences and unipotent/nilpotent Jordan decompositions determine sharp entry times, all primitive period populations, cumulative entrance shells and uniform orbit basins by the Fitting decomposition. A separate adjacency-mask implementation checked all 110 test size pairs and exhaustively checked complete state spaces for 36 pairs of size <=12, including each basin; full all-size proof is algebraic, not extrapolated from tests.

value.rationale: One added intra-shore edge reverses qualitatively the finite-field neighbor-parity dynamics: it changes an otherwise nilpotent update to one with nonzero recurrent structure in three arithmetic phases and creates precisely three genuine period-four orbits in the odd-odd phase, although the unedited biclique has no period-four orbits. Determining exact Jordan phases, temporal entrance shells, and individual basin sizes across every a>=3,b>=2 is a natural structural graph-perturbation question rather than a tiny tabular example or routine restatement. The proof isolates a four-dimensional defect subspace with uniform parity control, suitable for comparisons with other local graph edits.
